diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the periodic case, we take $\mathcal{V}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$, $\mathcal{C}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$,
In the periodic case, we additionally assume that the velocity and magnetic field have zero spatial mean.
for $\mathbf{v}\in H_{\mathrm{per}}^{1}(\Omega)^{2}$ with zero spatial mean in the periodic case.

issues.failure_explanation: In the periodic case the spaces are defined as V = C = H^1_per(Omega)^2 with conforming subspaces, which contain fields of nonzero spatial mean (e.g., nonzero constants), and for such fields ||v_h|| <= C||grad v_h|| fails (constant field: left side positive, right side zero). The paper itself states the estimate is used only 'on the subspace of periodic functions with zero spatial mean', yet then asserts it for all v_h in V_h, C_h in C_h. The only zero-mean hypothesis anywhere is on the exact solution (Assumption assu:regularity); nothing places the discrete solution or the error functions xi, psi in the zero-mean subspace, and the scheme as posed in Problem prob:fully does not preserve zero mean (tested with a constant, the momentum equation leaves l(a;b,1) = -1/2((div a)b,1) != 0 for non-discretely-solenoidal fields). Hence, in the periodic case, the forcing absorption |<f^n,u_h^n>| <= (2Re)^{-1}||grad u_h^n||^2 + C||f^n||^2_{H^{-1}} in the stability proof, and the Ladyzhenskaya/Poincare bounds on xi, psi in the convergence proof, use these inequalities outside their valid hypotheses.

failure_location.quote:
Therefore, in both
cases there exists a constant $C>0$, independent of $h$, such that
\[
\lVert\mathbf v_h\rVert \le C\lVert\nabla \mathbf v_h\rVert,\qquad
\lVert\mathbf C_h\rVert \le C\lVert\nabla \mathbf C_h\rVert
\]
for all $\mathbf v_{h}\in \mathcal{V}_{h}$ and $\mathbf C_{h}\in \mathcal{C}_{h}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the periodic case, pose the continuous and discrete problems in the zero-spatial-mean subspaces of H^1_per(Omega)^2 (standard for periodic flow); then every quoted Poincare/Ladyzhenskaya application is within its hypothesis class and the scheme, all estimates, and all rates are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: For periodic boundary conditions, the proofs of Theorem thm:stability (forcing absorption) and Theorem thm:convergence (Ladyzhenskaya/Poincare bounds on the error functions, e.g. in the nonlinear-term estimates) rely on inequalities that are false for the discrete fields as defined; as written, both results are fully justified only for homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, while the periodic vortex benchmark falls outside them.
issues.title: Periodic-case Poincare/Ladyzhenskaya inequalities applied to discrete fields not known to have zero mean
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local condition (zero-mean periodic spaces) that validates every affected inequality without altering the scheme, the method, any rate, or the advertised scope; no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
the stability analysis is based on the corrected
discrete memory functional $\mathcal{E}^{(\nu)}_{\phi,n}$ defined below, 
which provides a suitable estimate even when the fractional order 
function $\nu(t)$ is non-monotone.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is the paper's stability result, but the functional it bounds from above is not nonnegative, so the inequality yields no control of the solution. Assumption assu:orders_bounds allows increasing orders; take e.g. a uniform mesh with N=2, tau=1/2 and a continuous order with nu(t_1)=0.5, nu(t_2)=0.9: direct evaluation gives b^{(nu)}_{1,1} approx 0.7979, b^{(nu)}_{2,2} approx 0.9807, b^{(nu)}_{2,1} approx 0.0704, hence (delta^{(nu)}_{2,1})_+ = (b^{(nu)}_{2,2} - b^{(nu)}_{1,1})_+ approx 0.1829 and E^{(nu)}_{phi,2} = (1/2)(b^{(nu)}_{2,1} - (delta^{(nu)}_{2,1})_+)||phi^1||^2 + (1/2)b^{(nu)}_{2,2}||phi^2||^2 approx -0.0562||phi^1||^2 + 0.4904||phi^2||^2, which is negative whenever phi^2 = 0 and phi^1 != 0 (values compatible with the scheme for suitable forcing). The negative weights are O(1) while the dissipative terms on the left control ||phi^k||^2 only with a factor tau, so the negative part cannot be absorbed. Nonnegativity (or any lower bound) of E = Theta - R is never established and is false in general, so the argument proves only a bare inequality, materially weaker than the advertised stability estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive stability through the paper's own Groenwall route in the regime alpha(t) = beta(t): Lemma lem:frac1 gives (1/2) Delta^{alpha(t_n)}_tau(||u_h^n||^2 + ||B_h^n||^2) + dissipation <= C(||f^n||^2_{H^{-1}} + ||g^n||^2_{H^{-1}}), and Theorem 3.2 of the appendix (A1-A3 verified in Lemma lem:check_frac_assump, with lambda = 0) then yields the genuine a priori bound ||u_h^n||^2 + ||B_h^n||^2 <= C(data); alternatively, restrict the order profiles to a class for which E >= 0 can be proved (e.g., nonincreasing orders) and state that restriction.
issues.overall_effect: Stability of the fully discrete variable-order scheme -- advertised in the abstract ('stability is obtained using corrected discrete memory functionals'), in contribution (3), and in the claim that the functional 'provides a suitable estimate even when nu(t) is non-monotone' -- is not established; in particular no stability bound is obtained for increasing order profiles, which are used in the numerical tests. Theorem thm:convergence does not use this result and is not directly affected.
issues.title: Corrected memory functional can be negative, so the stability theorem yields no a priori bound
issues.why_classification: The advertised general variable-order stability is not delivered and the functional is genuinely indefinite, so the statement cannot be salvaged by sign arguments; but a recognizably comparable stability result, in the same regime as the convergence theorem, is recovered with tools already in the paper -- a contained nontrivial replacement argument with a limited regime loss rather than a collapse of the analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The Stokes projector acts on the pair (u,p): its standard H^1- and L^2-error bounds contain the pressure best-approximation error, so the stated bound ||psi_u|| + h||grad psi_u|| <= Ch^{l+1}||u^n||_{H^{l+1}} holds only under pressure regularity such as p in L^infty(0,T;H^l(Omega)). The same gap affects the time-increment bound ||psi_u^k - psi_u^{k-1}|| <= C tau h^{l+1} sup ||d_t u||_{H^{l+1}} used later in the proof, which additionally needs d_t p in L^infty(0,T;H^l). Assumption assu:regularity imposes regularity on u and B only; no pressure regularity appears anywhere in the paper, so the projection estimates entering Theorem thm:convergence are unestablished premises.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add standard pressure regularity to Assumption assu:regularity, e.g. p in L^infty(0,T;H^l(Omega)) and d_t p in L^infty(0,T;H^l(Omega)); the Stokes-projection estimate (eq:approximation_errors) and its increment analogue then hold as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The spatial approximation terms entering the error recursion of Theorem thm:convergence (||psi_u||, ||grad psi_u||, and the increments of psi_u used to bound the fractional projection error) are controlled by estimates that do not follow from the stated assumptions, so the spatial part of the convergence rate is unjustified as written.
issues.title: Stokes-projection error bounds used without any pressure regularity assumption
issues.why_classification: A one-line, standard hypothesis addition after which routine projection theory applies; every claim, rate, and the advertised scope survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the fully discrete momentum identity from the semidiscrete one and testing with v_h = xi_u^n produces the pressure error term -(p^n - p_h^n, div xi_u^n) = -(psi_p^n, div xi_u^n) - (xi_p^n, div xi_u^n). Only the second part vanishes (the error mass equation gives (div xi_u^n, q_h) = 0 for q_h in Q_h); the first part equals -(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) by the Stokes-projector definition and is not zero. No pressure term appears in (eq:conv_step2), so the displayed error identity is not valid as written. The omitted term satisfies |(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n)| <= (eps/Re)||grad xi_u^n||^2 + C||grad psi_u^n||^2, i.e., it is of a form already estimated in the proof, so the final inequality (eq:conv_step5) and the theorem's rate are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the term -(psi_p^n, div xi_u^n) in (eq:conv_step2) and estimate it via the projector identity -(psi_p^n, div xi_u^n) = -(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) <= (eps/Re)||grad xi_u^n||^2 + C||grad psi_u^n||^2.
issues.overall_effect: The central error identity of the convergence proof is incomplete; once the term is restored, the subsequent estimates and the conclusion of Theorem thm:convergence are unchanged.
issues.title: Pressure error term missing from the error identity (eq:conv_step2)
issues.why_classification: A single missing term whose bound is already of a form estimated in the proof; restoring it is a short local repair that changes no estimate, rate, or claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The tau^2 contribution to I_2 (and hence to R = C(h^{2l}+h^{2m}+tau^2)) stands for ||r_1^n||^2 + ||r_2^n||^2 with ||r_i^n|| = O(tau) taken from (eq:frac_replacement). An O(tau) consistency error of the (variable-order) L1 approximation requires control of the second time derivative of the solution: the truncation error is governed by the modulus of continuity of d_t of the solution, and with only d_t u, d_t B bounded in time (Assumption assu:regularity) no algebraic rate holds in general. The stated hypotheses therefore do not support the tau^2 term, so the first-order temporal rate claimed in Theorem thm:convergence is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption assu:regularity to include second-order time regularity, e.g. d_{tt}u, d_{tt}B in L^infty(0,T;L^2(Omega)^2) (the standard hypothesis under which the cited L1 formula (eq:frac_replacement) holds); then ||r_i^n|| = O(tau) and the proof stands unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The O(tau) temporal rate in Theorem thm:convergence -- and the claimed agreement with the measured first-order convergence in Tables tab:convtest1, tab:convtest2, tab:convtest3 -- rests on a consistency bound that the stated regularity does not imply.
issues.title: First-order temporal truncation invoked without sufficient time-regularity hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard second-order time-regularity hypothesis is a local condition; the cited truncation theory then applies, and the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope all survive without any new nontrivial lemma.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, the velocity divergence remains small, and for the magnetic field the cleaning step reduces the divergence substantially over the whole time interval.
After cleaning, it is reduced to the level of $10^{-8}$ for all considered profiles.

issues.failure_explanation: With the update B_h^n = B~_h^n - grad phi_h^n and (eq:elliptic) as written, testing against psi_h in Psi_h (periodic case, where boundary terms vanish) gives (div B_h^n, psi_h) = (div B~_h^n, psi_h) - (div grad phi_h^n, psi_h) = (div B~_h^n, psi_h) + (grad phi_h^n, grad psi_h) = 2(div B~_h^n, psi_h): the step doubles, rather than eliminates, the Psi_h-component of the discrete divergence. The Helmholtz-type projection the paper describes requires the opposite sign, (grad phi_h^n, grad psi_h) = -(div B~_h^n, psi_h) (equivalently, the update B_h^n = B~_h^n + grad phi_h^n). As written, the construction contradicts its stated purpose and the reported post-cleaning divergence reduction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the right-hand side of (eq:elliptic) to (grad phi_h^n, grad psi_h) = -(div B~_h^n, psi_h), or equivalently set B_h^n = B~_h^n + grad phi_h^n, so that the step is the stated divergence projection.
issues.overall_effect: Implemented literally, the cleaning step amplifies the magnetic divergence instead of reducing it, contradicting the reported numerical behavior (reduction from about 1e-4 before cleaning to about 1e-8 after cleaning); the guarantee implied by the text ('the cleaning step reduces the divergence substantially') fails for the procedure as written.
issues.title: Divergence-cleaning step is sign-inconsistent and amplifies the discrete divergence as written
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single sign in a standard projection step, and the intended behavior is confirmed by the paper's own reported results; no other claim, estimate, or guarantee depends on it.
